_about: The parity gate's configuration (tests/parity/compare.mjs). `gates` names what slice P2-09 owns: `full` routes are compared whole (landmarks, headings, controls, list fields, row heights at 375); `frame` routes only for the shell the slice draws (frameControls, frameHeadings); `pixelExact` routes also gate on the 2 percent pixel diff. `approved` lists the differences from the baseline that a ruling allows, each with its ruling; nothing else may differ. Later UI slices add their routes to `gates` in their own PR.

approved.ruling: shell-list.md section 8 (AppShell row) and ASSEMBLY H.1 B-0121/B-0153: /privacy and the auth routes render without the signed-in chrome; the old page drew the signed-in nav card and a second <main> for an anonymous visitor (a defect, not a design).
Same ruling: the nav card's wordmark heading is chrome.
Same ruling: the nav card, the top bar and the back-to-top button are signed-in chrome.
Same ruling: the article is a child of the page's single main, not a nested one; its row text is unchanged, its height differs with the removed chrome.
Same ruling: the nav card is absent, so the page is not pixel-exact; structure and copy still gate.

Same as auth-field-height: / signed out lands on /login.
